messages:
Anya (Support): @channel :rotating_light: Heads up — customer acme-prod opened an escalation. p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~120ms to ~2.3s starting ~02:00 UTC. They attached traces showing many requests sitting in the continuous-batcher waiting for ~2s before being released. They say it started after a config change last week but unsure which. Can SRE/eng take a look?

Vik (Eng): Thanks @Anya. Can you paste the route and model they hit and any headers? Also do we have the batcher config for that route?

Anya (Support): Route: prod-gen-us, model: redwood/gpt-small-8k:1. Headers show client app version 3.4.1 and a custom routing tag x-cust-type:small. No obvious auth or quota errors. Customer reports traffic pattern is many small requests (avg prompt tokens ~20) but at low QPS (~4rps). They attached logs with the batcher hold durations.

Maria (SRE): I pulled metrics from the batcher telemetry for prod-gen-us. Key findings:
- median batch_hold_ms ~ 12ms
- p95 batch_hold_ms ~ 220ms
- p99 batch_hold_ms ~ 1.98s (spike aligned with customer incidents)
- avg batch_size during spike ~ 3 (we're waiting for configured max_batch_size 32)

Looks like max_wait_ms is being hit frequently when QPS is low and max_batch_size high -> tail latency due to waiting for batch to fill. Showing config from route manifest:
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_size: 32
  max_wait_ms: 2000
  early_release_pct: 0

Maria (SRE): Repro steps I used locally (reliable):
1) Run 4 rps client hitting prod-gen-us with short prompts (20 tokens) for 5m
2) Observe batch_hold histogram in /metrics
3) p99 spikes to ~2s when inter-arrival > (32 requests / target throughput) and max_wait_ms is reached

Leo (ML Eng): That config is aggressive for low QPS customers. It's tuned for high throughput to save tokens at scale. For low QPS, it increases cold tail since we wait for batch to fill. We should either lower max_wait_ms or enable early_release so small batches forward sooner.

Vik (Eng): Agreed. Two immediate questions: what's the impact on token cost/throughput if we lower wait? and can we do a quick temporary mitigation that doesn't require full rollout?

Maria (SRE): Quick mitigation options (ranked):
1) Per-route override: set max_wait_ms=100 for prod-gen-us (low risk, instant)
2) Enable early_release_pct:50 (allow batches to go when 50% full) — medium risk for quality/economics
3) Add a small QPS-aware policy (if observed qps<10 then switch to small-batch profile)

I'll push option 1 as a canary to 10% first. If that looks good we roll to 100%.

Anya (Support): Customer is OK with a temporary config change if it reduces latency. They prefer a short-term fix rather than waiting for an infra change.

Maria (SRE): Applying canary now.

deploy-bot: config-change triggered by maria: PATCH /routes/prod-gen-us -> {"continuous_batcher":{"max_wait_ms":100}}. Canary target: 10% of nodes. Rolling.

deploy-bot: canary applied to 3/30 nodes (10%).

Maria (SRE): Monitoring p99 across the canary nodes — initial graphs show p99 on canary nodes dropped from ~2.1s -> 180ms within 30s. No error increase.

Vik (Eng): Nice. Any throughput regressions / increased token usage on the canary? We need to quantify cost impact.

Maria (SRE): Token/unit throughput for canary: small increase ~3% due to slightly smaller average batch size (was 3->1.9). Throughput (requests/sec served) steady. Given customer priority, 3% cost bump is acceptable.

Anya (Support): Customer confirmed latency improved within minutes on their test traffic. They asked whether this change will be permanent or if there is an automated remit.

Leo (ML Eng): For longer term: we should add an adaptive tuner that adjusts max_wait_ms or switches batch profiles based on measured inter-arrival percentiles. Also add a per-route default we can toggle from Console for support.

Maria (SRE): Agreed. Next actions I'm adding:
- Roll canary to 100% (if no regressions in 5m)
- Create an alert on continuous_batcher.batch_hold_ms p99 > 500ms for any route
- Add a small doc for support: how to triage batcher wait issues and quick commands
- Open a tracking ticket to add adaptive-tuner (owner: Leo)

Vik (Eng): Before rolling to 100% let's run a synthetic soak for 10m at 4rps against entire service to confirm no downstream saturation.

Maria (SRE): Running soak now. Command used:
load-test --target https://prod-gen-us.redwood/api/v1/generate --qps 4 --duration 600 --prompt-file short_prompts.txt


deploy-bot: Canary 100% applied. Change rolled to all nodes.

Maria (SRE): Post-roll stats (1m after): p99 overall dropped from 2.1s -> 190ms; p95 from 220ms -> 90ms. Batch_hold p99 dropped to 210ms. No increase in 5xx or queue rejections.

Anya (Support): Customer notified and happy. They requested a follow-up that explains why this happened and what we will change permanently.

Maria (SRE): Draft of follow-up explanation I sent to customer (short): "We identified the continuous-batcher for your route was set to wait up to 2000ms to build large batches (32), which is efficient at high QPS but causes tail latency for low QPS, small-request workflows. We temporarily lowered the wait to 100ms to reduce tail latency. We're implementing an adaptive profile so routes with low QPS will use smaller wait/batch settings automatically."

Vik (Eng): For postmortem notes: root cause = mismatch between batcher defaults (throughput-optimized) and customer's request pattern (low-QPS, small prompts). Contributing factors: lack of per-route alerting on batch_hold p99 and no auto tuning.

Leo (ML Eng): I'll own the adaptive-tuner ticket. Proposal highlights:
- observe inter-arrival 1/5/15m percentiles
- if median inter-arrival > X ms, reduce max_wait_ms and batch_size
- should be conservative: start with non-invasive profile and can be overridden manually

Maria (SRE): Adding ticket and linking this thread. Also creating support playbook page: "batcher-tail-latency-troubleshooting" with commands and metrics queries.

Anya (Support): Closing the customer escalation as resolved for now. I'll keep thread open until the adaptive ticket lands.

Vik (Eng): Thanks everyone. Small suggestion: add a Console toggle for support to flip to "low-latency" batch profile per-route — reduces future blips.

Maria (SRE): Noted. I'll include that in the ticket.

-- end of thread --
